reason: Successor authorization for Controller State V5.363 after the sole successor Full Windows UAT froze on FIRST RED: the desktop shortcut still displayed the retired teal frontend icon. Evidence audit proves one native identity boundary with two same-root defects: formal Final Builder does not consume the existing assertBranding() PE readback verifier on the actual final Yance.exe, and NSIS replaces the same installed executable/shortcut paths without notifying the mature Windows Shell cache authority through SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_UPDATEITEM, SHCNF_PATH, ...). This authorization preserves canonical assets/branding/yance as the only brand SSOT, pinned rcedit/NSIS as native materialization mechanics, and Windows Shell as cache/display authority. No shortcut-specific icon authority, cache helper, fallback, mirror state, new dependency, or second lifecycle is introduced.

requiredClosure: Formal Final Builder must consume existing tools/wp7/pe-resource-editor.js assertBranding() on the actual materialized Yance.exe before PASS/seal, including embedded RT_ICON equality to canonical assets/branding/yance/generated/Yance.ico and existing VERSIONINFO/code-image checks.
Formal Final Builder must also read back the final NSIS installer RT_ICON through existing PE icon extraction functions and prove it equals the same canonical ICO before PASS/seal.

NSIS must preserve shortcut target/DisplayIcon authority on installed Yance.exe and, after transactional promotion plus shortcut/registry creation, notify the mature Windows Shell of changed same-path items using SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_UPDATEITEM, SHCNF_PATH, ...).

Notify installed Yance.exe, desktop shortcut and Start Menu product shortcut only; do not use SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED, broad cache demolition, shortcut-specific icon files, custom icon cache state or helper-owned lifecycle.
Existing tests must fail if final PE readback is omitted, if retired frontend/assets/icon.* re-enters the production path, or if the NSIS shell-update notification is removed.

Before Exact Head, local/materialized proof must cover final Yance.exe RT_ICON, installer RT_ICON, desktop/Start Menu shortcut authority, Apps & Features DisplayIcon, Tray/BrowserWindow canonical alias, and no retired icon authority in the production chain.

reviewedCandidates.name: Existing WP7 PE branding verifier
reviewedCandidates.reason: It already reads actual PE resources, compares embedded RT_ICON content with the approved ICO, validates VERSIONINFO and preserves Electron code-image trust. The correct fix is to consume it in Final Builder, not create a second PE parser.

reviewedCandidates.name: Windows Shell change-notification authority
reviewedCandidates.reason: Windows Shell owns item/icon caching. The narrow public seam for an existing item whose cached data changed is SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_UPDATEITEM, SHCNF_PATH, fullpath, NULL).

reviewedCandidates.name: NSIS installer mechanics
reviewedCandidates.reason: NSIS remains responsible only for transactional install, registry/shortcut creation and platform notification after those writes.

reviewedCandidates.name: Canonical Yance branding authority
reviewedCandidates.reason: The canonical generated ICO and runtime alias are byte-identical and remain the sole icon source for EXE, installer, Tray and BrowserWindow.

retireOrAvoid: Do not reintroduce frontend/assets/icon.ico or frontend/assets/icon.png into any production materialization path.
Do not add shortcut-specific icon files or a third brand asset authority.
Do not implement a custom Windows icon cache, cache state file, retry loop, Explorer restart, ie4uinit helper, or broad icon-cache deletion.
Do not use SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED for this item update; consume the narrow SHCNE_UPDATEITEM seam.
Do not create a second PE parser/verifier; consume existing assertBranding/extractIconImageSet tooling.

authorityPreservation.peMaterializationOwner: pinned rcedit plus existing WP7 Final Builder

localAcceptance: Changed paths are exactly the four implementation paths and no others.
Final Builder cannot return PASS unless actual materialized Yance.exe embedded RT_ICON matches canonical generated Yance.ico through existing assertBranding().
Final Builder cannot return PASS unless actual materialized installer embedded RT_ICON image set matches the same canonical generated Yance.ico through existing PE extraction tooling.

NSIS keeps desktop/Start Menu shortcuts and Apps & Features DisplayIcon bound to installed Yance.exe and emits narrow SHCNE_UPDATEITEM notifications for the installed executable and recreated product shortcuts after transactional commit.
No production-code reference to frontend/assets/icon.* exists.
Existing canonical alias verification remains GREEN and no second brand authority is added.
Focused WP7 branding/final-builder tests, source regressions, verify:wp0 and WP7 source closure are GREEN before Exact Head.
Final materialized Windows proof reads the actual PE resources before promotion.
